detailed_rationale:
Indian Overseas Bank continues a genuine multi-year turnaround. Q3 FY26 (Dec 2025) net interest income was Rs 4,874 Cr with net profit of Rs 1,427 Cr, and FY26 full-year revenue and profit came in at Rs 31,896 Cr and Rs 5,418 Cr respectively, with a 5-year profit CAGR the data shows at roughly 48% off a low post-PCA (Prompt Corrective Action) base. Asset quality is now genuinely strong for a PSU bank: Gross NPA of 1.33% and Net NPA of just 0.18% as of Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026), down from 2.14%/0.37% a year earlier -- a level that would be respectable even against private-sector peers, let alone the historically NPA-heavy PSU cohort IOB itself came from. CARE reaffirmed A1+ on certificates of deposit and upgraded Tier-II bonds to AA+ with a stable outlook in July 2026, external validation of the credit improvement.

Per our financial-sector convention, we do not treat IOB's balance-sheet leverage as a red flag (that is the banking business model); the metrics that matter are asset quality, capital and margin trajectory, and on the asset-quality dimension the bank is now performing well. Government ownership has declined only slowly (94.6% to 92.4% over the past year) and remains far above the 75% public-float requirement that PSU banks must eventually meet -- this is a known, slow-moving overhang (continued government stake sales over time) rather than a near-term catalyst risk, and it is the standard situation across most PSU banks, not IOB-specific.

We could not source CRAR or NIM figures directly from the data available to us this round, which we flag honestly rather than fabricate -- but the combination of strong and improving asset quality, sustained profit growth and external rating upgrades is a coherent enough picture to support the existing Hold call without needing those additional data points to reach a conclusion.
recommendation_rationale: Hold, matching the quant score -- genuinely improving asset quality (GNPA/NNPA both roughly halved year-on-year) and strong profit growth support at least a Hold; we do not have a basis to argue for anything more or less constructive than what the quant framework already assigns.
summary: Indian Overseas Bank, a public-sector bank, continues a multi-year recovery: asset quality has improved sharply (gross bad loans down to about 1.3% of the book, from over 2% a year ago) and profit grew strongly through FY26, with rating agencies upgrading the bank's bond ratings. Government ownership remains high and will likely be reduced gradually over time to meet listing rules, a modest and well-flagged overhang rather than a new risk. We rate it a Hold.
positive_para: Asset quality has improved markedly (Gross NPA roughly halved to 1.33%, Net NPA down to 0.18%), profit growth has been strong and sustained, and external validation is coming through (CARE upgraded Tier-II bonds to AA+, reaffirmed A1+ on CDs). This is a credible, ongoing PSU-bank turnaround rather than an early-stage or unproven one.
negative_para: We could not verify current CRAR or net interest margin figures from the sources available this round, which limits how precisely we can judge capital buffers and margin durability -- a data gap we flag rather than paper over. Government ownership at ~92% is still well above the 75% public-float requirement, meaning further stake sales are a matter of when, not if, which will be a recurring modest supply overhang on the stock for several years.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A PSU bank turnaround story with genuinely improving asset quality (sub-1.5% GNPA) and strong profit growth deserves credit, but PSU banks structurally carry lower sustainable ROE than top private banks and face a persistent government-stake-sale overhang; the current valuation should reflect a 'good, recovering PSU bank' rather than a 'best-in-class private bank' multiple. On the asset-quality trend alone this looks like a fair, unexciting Hold rather than either a bargain or a rich multiple.
